unit_label: Module A: International Banking - Facilities for Exporters and Importers

facts.statement: Export trade is regulated by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, which announces the policies and procedures for exports; authorised dealer banks conduct export transactions in conformity with the Foreign Trade Policy, the rules framed by the Government and the directions of the Reserve Bank. The Reserve Bank, under FEMA, regulates the exchange control side, receipts and payments of foreign exchange; DGFT regulates the trade control side through the Foreign Trade Policy.
facts.locator: Part A, A.1; S03 printed p. 126, section 5.1

facts.statement: Every person or firm engaged in export-import trade must obtain an Importer-Exporter Code number from the DGFT and quote it in declarations and forms; an exporter of services registers with the Services Export Promotion Council or the Federation of Indian Export Organisations, and an exporter of software registers with the Software Technology Park of India.

Exports of goods are declared on the Export Declaration Form (EDF) and exports of software in non-physical form on the SOFTEX form. The declaration requirement does not apply to the cases in Regulation 4 of the Export Regulations, but the exporter is still liable to realise and repatriate the proceeds as per FEMA regulations.
facts.locator: Part B, B.12; S03 printed pp. 127-128, section 5.2.2

facts.statement: If an exporter presents documents after the prescribed period of 21 days from the date of export, an authorised dealer may handle them without prior RBI approval if it is satisfied with the reasons for the delay.

The period for realisation and repatriation of export proceeds is nine months from the date of export for all exporters, including units in SEZs, status holder exporters, EOUs and units in EHTPs, STPs and BTPs, until further notice. For goods exported to a warehouse established outside India the proceeds must be realised within fifteen months from the date of shipment, and for goods exported to Bharat Mart within nine months from the date of sale of the goods from the warehouse. The period was lengthened to fifteen months by an amendment of 13 November 2025 and restored to nine months by an amendment of 5 June 2026.
facts.locator: Part A, A.2 and its footnotes 5 and 6; S03 printed p. 129

facts.statement: An authorised dealer may extend the period for realisation by up to six months at a time, irrespective of the invoice value, if the export transactions are not under investigation by the Directorate of Enforcement, the CBI or other agencies, the bank is satisfied the exporter could not realise the proceeds for reasons beyond its control, and the exporter declares the proceeds will be realised in the extended period. Where the extension goes beyond one year from the date of export, the exporter's total outstanding must not exceed USD one million or 10 per cent of average export realisations in the preceding three financial years, whichever is higher; where the exporter has filed suit abroad against the buyer, extension may be granted irrespective of the amount. Cases not covered need prior approval of the Regional Office of RBI, and the extension is reported in EDPMS.
facts.locator: Part C, C.20; S03 printed pp. 133-134

facts.statement: For prepayment of usance bills a cash discount may be allowed up to the proportionate interest on the unexpired period of usance, at the rate in the export contract or, if none, at the prime rate, a benchmark or another widely accepted reference rate of the invoice currency. In other cases, after a bill has been negotiated or sent for collection, an authorised dealer may approve a reduction in invoice value if satisfied of genuineness and provided the reduction does not exceed 25 per cent of the invoice value, is not for commodities with floor price stipulations, the exporter is not on the RBI exporters' caution list and the exporter is advised to surrender proportionate export incentives. For exporters with more than three years in export business and a satisfactory track record, meaning outstanding exports not above 5 per cent of average annual export realisation in the preceding three financial years, no percentage ceiling applies.
facts.locator: Part C, C.16 and C.17; S03 pp. 132-133

facts.statement: An authorised dealer may allow agency commission by remittance or deduction from the invoice value if the commission has been declared on the EDF or SOFTEX form and accepted by customs, or, if not declared, after satisfying itself about the reasons and that a valid agreement exists, and the relevant shipment has been made. Commission is prohibited on exports by Indian partners as equity participation in an overseas joint venture or wholly owned subsidiary and on exports under the Rupee Credit Route except up to 10 per cent of invoice value for tea and tobacco.
facts.locator: Part D, D.1; S03 printed p. 132

facts.statement: The authorised dealer through which export proceeds were realised may consider refund of proceeds for goods re-imported because of poor quality, after due diligence on the exporter's track record and the bona fides of the transaction, and obtaining a certificate from DGFT or customs that no export incentive was availed or that proportionate incentives have been surrendered; re-import need not be insisted on where the goods were auctioned or destroyed by the authorities.
facts.locator: Part D, D.2; S03 printed p. 133 states a three-month re-import undertaking

facts.statement: Asian Clearing Union participants may settle in ACU Dollar, ACU Euro or ACU Japanese Yen; Indo-Myanmar trade may be settled in any freely convertible currency in addition to the ACU mechanism; current account transactions with Iran and with Sri Lanka may be settled in any permitted currency outside the ACU mechanism.
facts.locator: Part A, A.3(iv); S03 printed pp. 130-131 lists the ACU arrangement without the Sri Lanka relaxation

facts.statement: Where an exporter receives an advance payment from a buyer abroad, shipment must be made within three years of receipt of the advance, any interest on the advance must not exceed the benchmark or reference rate plus 100 basis points, and the shipping documents must be routed through the authorised dealer through which the advance was received.

payload.title: Two sets of rules for every export: exchange control and trade control
payload.core_explanation_md:
An exporter answers to two regulators for different things.

- **Trade control** (what may be exported, how, with which incentives): the **Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)**, under the Ministry of Commerce, through the **Foreign Trade Policy**.
- **Exchange control** (how the foreign money comes back): the **Reserve Bank of India**, under **FEMA**. Authorised dealer banks carry it out.

The key that opens both is the **Importer-Exporter Code (IEC)** from the DGFT, quoted in every declaration and form. Exporters of **services** also register with the **Services Export Promotion Council** or the **Federation of Indian Export Organisations**, and exporters of **software** with the **Software Technology Park of India**.

payload.title: EDF, SOFTEX and the two clocks an exporter lives by
payload.core_explanation_md:
**What is declared**: goods go on the **Export Declaration Form (EDF)**; software sent in non-physical form goes on the **SOFTEX** form. A few cases are **exempt** from declaring (listed in Regulation 4 of the Export Regulations), but the exporter must still **realise and repatriate the proceeds**.

**Clock 1: submit documents within 21 days** of the export. If late, the authorised dealer may still handle them **without prior RBI approval** if it is satisfied with the reasons.

**Clock 2: realise the money within nine months** of the export, for all exporters including SEZ units, status holders, EOUs and units in EHTPs, STPs and BTPs.
- **Warehouse abroad**: proceeds within **fifteen months** of shipment.
- **Bharat Mart**: **nine months** from the date of sale of the goods from the warehouse.

The period went to **fifteen months** in November 2025 and was **restored to nine months** on 5 June 2026, so **nine months** applies at the exam cut-off.

payload.title: When the money is late: extending the realisation period
payload.core_explanation_md:
The exporter applies to the authorised dealer. The bank may extend by **up to six months at a time**, whatever the invoice value, if **all** of these hold:

1. The exports are **not under investigation** by the Directorate of Enforcement, the CBI or other agencies.
2. The bank is satisfied the delay is for **reasons beyond the exporter's control**.
3. The exporter **declares** the proceeds will be realised in the extended period.
4. If the extension goes **beyond one year** from export, the exporter's **total outstanding** is within **USD 1 million or 10% of average export realisation in the last three financial years, whichever is higher**.

If the exporter has **sued the buyer abroad**, extension may be given **whatever the amount**. Cases outside these rules need **prior RBI Regional Office approval**. Every extension is **reported in EDPMS**.

payload.title: Cutting an invoice after shipment: two routes, with different limits
Commission, refunds and advances: what the bank checks
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Agency commission**: paid by remittance or by deduction from the invoice. The bank checks it was **declared on the EDF or SOFTEX** and accepted by customs (or, if not, why, and that a **valid agreement** exists) and that the **shipment has been made**. **Prohibited** on exports as equity in an overseas joint venture or wholly owned subsidiary, and on **Rupee Credit Route** exports except up to **10% of invoice value for tea and tobacco**.

**Refund of export proceeds**: allowed through the bank that realised them, for goods **re-imported for poor quality**, after due diligence, the bank checking that **no export incentive** was availed or it has been **surrendered**. Re-import need not be insisted on where the goods were **auctioned or destroyed** by the authorities.

**Advance from the buyer**: **ship within three years**, interest **not above the benchmark rate plus 100 basis points**, and the **documents routed through the bank that received the advance**.

payload.title: Settling with neighbours: the Asian Clearing Union and the exceptions
payload.core_explanation_md:
The **Asian Clearing Union (ACU)** lets member countries settle eligible payments in **ACU Dollar**, **ACU Euro** or **ACU Japanese Yen**, each equal in value to **one US dollar, euro or yen**. Banks keep these accounts with correspondents in other member countries.

Exceptions to remember:
- **Myanmar**: any freely convertible currency **in addition to** the ACU mechanism.
- **Iran** and **Sri Lanka**: eligible current account transactions, including trade, may be settled in **any permitted currency outside the ACU mechanism**.

Older books list the whole ACU group without the Sri Lanka relaxation. The Reserve Bank's current Master Direction is the authority.

payload.title: Tracing the dates of a late export bill
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: an exporter ships goods on 10 January 2026. The bill is unpaid. The buyer is facing a dispute and the exporter cannot collect. Assume the export is not under investigation and the exporter's total outstanding is small. What are the key dates?

worked_steps.description: Documents should reach the bank within 21 days of export.
Realisation deadline: nine months from the export date.
A first extension of up to six months from that deadline.
The point beyond which the one-year outstanding test applies is one year from export.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Documents by 31 January 2026; proceeds by 10 October 2026; a first extension can reach 10 April 2027, and since that is beyond 10 January 2027 the outstanding test (USD 1 million or 10% of average realisation) must be met

self_check.prompt_text: If the exporter had been a status holder in a Special Economic Zone, would the nine-month period change?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: the nine-month period covers all exporters, including SEZ units and status holders.

payload.stem_md: An exporter's usance bill for USD 80,000 has 45 days of the usance period unexpired when the buyer prepays it. The contract provides interest at 6% per annum on a 360-day basis. What is the maximum cash discount, in USD?

numeric_rule.rounding_instruction: Give the answer to 2 decimal places.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Maximum discount is the interest on the unexpired period: 80,000 × 6% × 45 ÷ 360 = 600.00.

worked_solution_steps.description: Interest for 45 days at 6% on a 360-day year

payload.stem_md: Which body announces the policies and procedures for exports from India, under the Foreign Trade Policy?

options.text_md: The Reserve Bank of India
options.explanation_md: RBI regulates the exchange control side.

options.text_md: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT)
options.explanation_md: DGFT regulates the trade control side.

options.text_md: The International Chambers of Commerce
options.explanation_md: The ICC publishes rules and guides, not national policy.

options.text_md: FEDAI
options.explanation_md: FEDAI is a self-regulatory body for forex dealers.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The DGFT, under the Ministry of Commerce, announces export policy and procedures; RBI handles the exchange control side.

payload.stem_md: What is the period for realisation and repatriation of export proceeds at the 30 June 2026 cut-off, for an exporter in a Software Technology Park?

options.text_md: Fifteen months from the date of export
options.explanation_md: That period applied between November 2025 and 5 June 2026.

options.text_md: Six months from the date of export
options.explanation_md: No such period applies.

options.text_md: Nine months from the date of export
options.explanation_md: The nine-month period covers STP units and all exporters.

options.text_md: Twenty-one days from the date of export
options.explanation_md: That is the period for submitting documents.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The period is nine months from the date of export for all exporters including STP units; the fifteen-month period of November 2025 was reversed on 5 June 2026.

payload.stem_md: An exporter presents documents to the authorised dealer 30 days after the date of export, for reasons the bank finds acceptable. What may the bank do?

options.text_md: Refuse, because 21 days is a hard limit
options.explanation_md: The dealer may accept after the period if it is satisfied.

options.text_md: Handle them only with prior RBI approval
options.explanation_md: Prior approval is not needed.

options.text_md: Handle them only if the exporter pays a penalty
options.explanation_md: No such penalty is stated.

options.text_md: Handle them without prior RBI approval
options.explanation_md: The dealer may handle late documents if satisfied with the reasons.

payload.correct_explanation_md: After the prescribed 21 days an authorised dealer may handle export documents without prior RBI approval if it is satisfied with the reasons for the delay.

payload.stem_md: The export proceeds of a shipment are overdue and the exporter has filed a suit abroad against the buyer. The delay is already beyond one year from export. How is the extension treated?

options.text_md: The dealer may grant extension irrespective of the amount outstanding
options.explanation_md: Where a suit has been filed against the buyer, the outstanding test does not apply.

options.text_md: The dealer may extend only if the outstanding is under USD 1 million
options.explanation_md: That test does not apply where a suit is filed.

options.text_md: Only the Reserve Bank may extend
options.explanation_md: The dealer may extend in this case.

options.text_md: No extension is possible beyond one year
options.explanation_md: Extensions beyond one year are possible under the conditions.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Where the exporter has filed suits abroad against the buyer, extension may be granted irrespective of the amount involved or outstanding.

payload.stem_md: After a bill has been negotiated, an exporter asks for a reduction of 30% in the invoice value. The exporter has three years' export experience, a satisfactory record and outstanding bills of 8% of average annual realisations over the last three financial years. What is the position?

options.text_md: The reduction can be approved without limit
options.explanation_md: Outstanding of 8% exceeds the 5% condition.

options.text_md: The ordinary 25% ceiling applies and the 30% cut exceeds it, because outstanding is above 5%
options.explanation_md: The no-ceiling relaxation needs outstanding not above 5% and more than three years in business.

options.text_md: The reduction can be approved up to 50%
options.explanation_md: No such limit applies.

options.text_md: The reduction is not possible under any circumstances
options.explanation_md: Up to 25% could be approved, subject to conditions.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The relaxation from the 25% ceiling needs more than three years in business and outstanding not above 5% of average annual realisation; at 8% the 25% ceiling applies.

payload.stem_md: On which of these exports is payment of agency commission prohibited?

options.text_md: Exports of garments declared on an EDF
options.explanation_md: Commission declared on the EDF can be allowed.

options.text_md: Exports where the shipment has been made and an agreement exists
options.explanation_md: These conditions allow commission.

options.text_md: Exports by Indian partners as equity participation in an overseas joint venture
options.explanation_md: Commission is prohibited on these exports.

options.text_md: Exports of software on a SOFTEX form
options.explanation_md: Commission declared on SOFTEX can be allowed.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Commission is prohibited on exports by Indian partners as equity participation in an overseas JV or WOS, and on Rupee Credit Route exports except up to 10% for tea and tobacco.

payload.stem_md: An exporter seeks a refund of proceeds for goods re-imported because of poor quality. Which condition does the authorised dealer check?

options.text_md: That the exporter has repaid the buyer in rupees
options.explanation_md: No such condition is stated.

options.text_md: That the buyer has lodged a complaint with the Reserve Bank
options.explanation_md: No such condition is stated.

options.text_md: That the goods were exported to an ACU country
options.explanation_md: The refund is not limited to ACU countries.

options.text_md: That no export incentive was availed against the export, or the proportionate incentive has been surrendered
options.explanation_md: This is a condition for a refund.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The dealer obtains a certificate that no export incentive was availed, or the proportionate incentive has been surrendered, among other checks.

payload.stem_md: Which statement about ACU settlement is correct?

options.text_md: Eligible trade transactions with Sri Lanka may be settled in any permitted currency outside the ACU mechanism
options.explanation_md: This is a stated relaxation.

options.text_md: All trade with Sri Lanka must be settled in ACU Dollar
options.explanation_md: Sri Lanka is outside the ACU mechanism for eligible current account transactions.

options.text_md: ACU Dollar is worth ten US dollars
options.explanation_md: ACU Dollar equals one US dollar.

options.text_md: Trade with Myanmar cannot be settled outside ACU
options.explanation_md: Myanmar trade may also use freely convertible currency.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Eligible current account transactions with Sri Lanka may be settled in any permitted currency outside the ACU mechanism; ACU Dollar is equal in value to one US dollar.

payload.stem_md: An Indian exporter receives an advance of USD 200,000 from a foreign buyer. Within how long must the goods be shipped?

options.text_md: Within nine months from receipt of the advance
options.explanation_md: Nine months is the realisation period for export proceeds.

options.text_md: Within one year from receipt of the advance
options.explanation_md: One year was the earlier period.

options.text_md: Within three years from receipt of the advance
options.explanation_md: The shipment period for advances is three years.

options.text_md: Within 21 days from receipt of the advance
options.explanation_md: 21 days is the document submission period.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The exporter must ensure shipment within three years from the date of receipt of the advance payment.

payload.stem_md: Goods are shipped on 10 January 2026. By what date must export proceeds be realised under the nine-month rule?

options.text_md: 10 September 2026
options.explanation_md: That is eight months.

options.text_md: 10 October 2026
options.explanation_md: Nine months from 10 January is 10 October.

options.text_md: 10 November 2026
options.explanation_md: That is ten months.

options.text_md: 10 April 2027
options.explanation_md: That is fifteen months.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Nine months from 10 January 2026 is 10 October 2026.

unresolved: The RBI Master Direction page shows its last update as 17 July 2026, after the 30 June 2026 cut-off. That update changed only the INR trade settlement paragraph (footnote 18); the sections taught here are unchanged. The nine-month period was restored on 5 June 2026 (before the cut-off) after a fifteen-month period from 13 November 2025.
RBI's Directions on Export and Import of Goods and Services of 16 January 2026 come into force on 1 October 2026 and supersede this Master Direction; their substantive text was not retrieved.
The courseware's Regulation 4 exemption list for EDF (printed p. 128) is not taught item by item (the Master Direction refers to Regulation 4 without listing the cases).

The courseware's write-off limits (printed p. 134), foreign currency accounts (EEFC, DDA; printed p. 135) and the effective date of realisation (a FEDAI rule) are covered in the next batch or held back.

The courseware's INR trade settlement description (printed pp. 131-132) is not taught: the Master Direction paragraph was substituted on 17 July 2026, after the cut-off, and the arrangement at the cut-off was not separately verified.
The courseware's three-month re-import undertaking for refunds (printed p. 133) is not in the Master Direction fetched; the Master Direction's own conditions are taught.
Reviewer for this batch is the authoring agent; no independent or human review.
